item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing — Open Studio — Tue Aug 4, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and draw. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re

item.title: Mindful Masculinity Men’s Group — Wed Aug 5, 7:00 PM — The Space
item.description:
We Meet Bi-Weekly Every Other Wednesday | 7 – 8:30 pm | $15 August 5 , 2026 Through open dialogue, mindfulness, and other calming practices we quiet the mind, open the heart, and deepen our connection to ourselves and each other. The meetings are hosted by Leo, mindfulness coach, teacher, and dad. We start by sharing our wins and challenges, honoring each voice without judgment or advice. We dive into practices that help us release stress, shift perspectives, and bring awareness and resilience into our lives. Each week, we focus on a different topic to help guide our lives. Together, we explore themes of trust, accomplishments, family, rest, intimacy, and presence — discovering new ways to move through the world as mindful men. Come as you are. Leave more grounded, connected, and inspired. Connect with Leo and the group on Instagram @holdingpresence
Source: The Space For Art

item.title: Art Lounge: Collage Night — Thu Aug 13, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Pull up a chair, pour yourself a drink, and make something beautiful! Art Lounge is your laid-back Thursday night creative escape — no agenda, no pressure, no experience needed. Just good music, great company, and a table full of materials waiting to become something entirely your own. Cut, tear, layer, and arrange your way through the evening at whatever pace feels right. Not sure where to start? We’ve got prompts to spark your imagination and get the ideas flowing. Or ignore them completely and follow your instincts – either way works perfectly here. Bring your friends, bring your BYOB, and leave with a piece of art you actually made. It’s the best kind of Thursday night. 🗓 Thursday, August 13 | 7:00 pm – 8:30 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, 2nd Floor, Montclair, NJ 🎟 $10 | All materials provided | BYOB welcome Open to everyone. No art experience needed. Just show up and create.
Source: The Space For Art

item.title: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again - Assemblage Art Exhibit Opening — Fri Aug 14, 5:00 PM
item.description: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again – Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg Opening Reception: Friday, August 14, 5 – 8pm The Space presents Unrecyclable: Look Again, a solo exhibition of assemblage art by Andrew Borg composed predominantly of the unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites he refused to throw away for nearly two years — the molded trays, caps, and packaging inserts that carry no recycling code and vanish into the trash without a thought. The exhibition, culminating Borg’s year as Artist in Residence at The Space, is on view August 14–22, 2026, with an opening reception Friday, August 14, from 5 to 8pm. What began as an act of defiance gradually became an act of appreciation: these are highly engineered, purpose-built objects, molded to cushion, position, and protect — aesthetic objects in their own right, designed by someone, meant to be forgotten by everyone. item.title: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg — Sat Aug 22, 1:00 PM
item.description: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg Closing Event for “Unrecyclable: Look Again” What do you see when you really look at what you throw away? Join artist Andrew Borg for the closing event of Unrecyclable: Look Again — an afternoon that begins with a gallery talk and ends with your hands deep in materials you never thought twice about discarding. After walking through the exhibition and sharing the story behind his two-year collection of unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites, Borg leads an immersive hands-on Assemblage Lab in which participants get to experience the process firsthand. Using unrecyclable packaging, abandoned electronics, appliances, and other “ghost objects,” you’ll build your own assemblage, sculpture, or mixed-media artwork — guided by the same impulse that drove this exhibition: look again. No artistic experience required. No right or wrong. Just a fresh set of eyes and a willingness to see the overlooked as raw material for something new. Unrec

item.title: Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop — Sun Aug 23, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop What if the Tarot could speak in your voice? In this exploratory workshop, we’ll dive into the rich history and symbolism of the Major Arcana — exploring the colors, archetypes, and allegories that have given these iconic cards their power for centuries. Then, we’ll turn that wisdom over to your own creative instincts. No art experience needed. No tarot experience needed. Just an open mind and a willingness to listen to what’s stirring inside you. You’ll choose a card that calls to you, journal your reflections, and then bring it to life through drawing, painting, or collage — reimagining it through your own symbols, style, and personal expression. The goal isn’t perfection; it’s presence. We’re letting intuition lead. 📅 Sunday, August 23 | 12:00 pm – 3:00 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Loft #2, Montclair, NJ 🎟 $50 | Returning participants: $30 (arrive at 1:30 pm) What You’ll Do:

We'll talk about Jones's conversation as well as "Kin," a poignant historical novel set in the civil rights era about two motherless childhood friends who take very different journeys: one to the storied HBCU Spellman College, the other to make her way in the world.
TAYARI JONES is the author of four others novels, most recently the New York Times bestseller "An American Marriage," which was an Oprah’s Book Club selection and also appeared on Barack Obama’s summer reading list and his year-end roundup. item.title: Classic Films Now: Network — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Run Time: 121 Minutes. Recommended for ages 18+ A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. Best Picture nominee about a mentally unstable news anchor who, after being told he’s to be fired, becomes a media superstar when he begins delivering nightly rants and threatens an on-air suicide for his final broadcast. Paddy Chayevsky’s script won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay; Peter Firth received a posthumous Best Actor award as the unhinged newsman; and Faye Dunaway won Best Actress as a scheming network exec.
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. item.description:

Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

item.title: The First Birds of Autumn NEW — Wed Sep 2, 8:00 AM — Montclair - Offsite
item.description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
We will visit a different site each week to witness the southbound migration of birds from as far away as Alaska and the Russian Far East. Vireos, warblers, and tanagers are among the songbirds likely to be seen in August and September, along with a good range of wading birds. Our destinations will be set shortly before each excursion, the choice determined by recent reports of concentrations of migrants.
